mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive due to lower real borrowing costs encouraging equity investment.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the CPIAUCSL inflation index above 3% in a month signals aggressive monetary policy tightening, which tends to depress equity valuations and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3.0 by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns remain positive despite inflation spike (p-value > 0.05 in a two-sample test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS (labor market activity) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests a tight labor market, which is associated with higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for two consecutive months and UNRATE decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 5-day horizon, SPX 20-day forward return is negative or statistically indistinguishable from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) unexpectedly exceeds its prior quarter trend by at least 2 percentage points, it signals resilient supply-side momentum that tends to boost investor confidence and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO quarter-over-quarter growth > +2.0 percentage points surprise
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the INDPRO surprise (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month decline in RSAFS (retail sales) accompanied by a sustained drop in HOUST (housing starts) indicates weakening demand-side conditions that often precede equity drawdowns; this mechanism predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls for three consecutive months and HOUST falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 60-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in monthly PAYEMS accompanied by a sharp drop in UNRATE (unemployment rate) creates a labor market imbalance that tends to raise wage growth expectations and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a single month and UNRATE falls by >0.5 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward return is negative despite the labor market imbalance (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged period of declining FEDFUNDS rates without a corresponding rise in CPIAUCSL inflation, the S&P 500 forward 5-day return tends to be positive as the real interest rate continues to decline, lowering discount rates on expected cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases for four consecutive months and CPIAUCSL remains below 2.0% for the same period
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward return is negative or flat over the 5-day horizon (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE remains above 4.5% for three consecutive months despite a modest uptick in INDPRO, it indicates weak labor absorption and muted economic recovery, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.5% for three consecutive months and INDPRO grows by <0.5 percentage points over the same period
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive or statistically indistinguishable from zero (p > 0.05).
